Declare a Kaplan-Meier curve

Source: R/ggplot2_survival_declaration.R
maidr_survival.Rd

maidr_survival() draws Kaplan-Meier survival curves – one per stratum, each held level until an event drops it – and declares them as such, so that maidr reads them as a survival layer: each time announced with its survival estimate and, when the band is drawn, its confidence interval, the times a subject was censored marked so a reader can step between them with the rotor, and the median survival of each curve in the description. The same staircase drawn with geom_step() reads as a step chart, which announces the levels and nothing of the censoring that says how much of the curve the data still supports.

Give it a survival::survfit object and it draws the curves plot() of that object would: ggplot() + maidr_survival(fit). Give it data and aesthetics and it draws them as they are, as any geom does.

The survival layer type [experimental] is one of the experimental plot types: it has not been through a user study, and its reading may change without a deprecation period. See "Experimental Plot Types" in the README.

Usage

maidr_survival(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  conf.int = FALSE,
  conf.int.alpha = 0.2,
  censor = TRUE,
  censor.shape = 3,
  censor.size = 3,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Aesthetics, as for ggplot2::geom_step(): x (the time) and y (the survival estimate) are required, and ymin, ymax and censored may be mapped as described in Details. Or a survfit object, drawn as described there.

data

The layer's data, as for ggplot2::geom_step(), or a survfit object. When mapping is the survfit object, data may be further aesthetics.

position

Position adjustment, as for ggplot2::geom_step().

...

Other arguments passed to the layer, such as linewidth or a fixed colour – except stat, which is fixed at "identity".

conf.int

Whether to draw the confidence band from ymin and ymax (from the object's own bounds, for a survfit), and read it as each point's yMin and yMax. FALSE by default.

conf.int.alpha

The band's opacity.

censor

Whether to draw a mark at each censored time. Censoring is read either way.

censor.shape, censor.size

The marks' plotting character and size, as shape and size are given to ggplot2::geom_point().

na.rm

If FALSE (the default), rows with missing values are removed with a warning.

show.legend

Whether this layer is included in the legends.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, the plot's default aesthetics are not inherited. Always FALSE for a survfit object.

Value

A ggplot2 layer, to be added to a plot with +.

From a survfit object

The curves start at the origin survival::survfit0() adds, as plot() starts them, and run to each stratum's last time. The layer draws from a data frame of its own, with the columns Time, Survival probability, lower, upper, censored and, for a fit with strata, Stratum, which are what the axes and the legend are titled by; map further aesthetics onto them, maidr_survival(fit, aes(linetype = Stratum)), and retitle with ggplot2::labs(). The plot's own aesthetics are not inherited. A multi-state fit, or one with several curves per stratum (survfit() of a Cox model over several new subjects), is an error: neither is one survival curve per stratum.

From data

x is the time and y the survival estimate, one row per time at which the estimate is reported, and the strata are groups, split by colour, linetype or group as the series of a line chart are. censored marks the times a subject left the study without the event: TRUE, or a count greater than zero such as a survfit summary's n.censor. ymin and ymax are the band's bounds at each time, drawn and read only with conf.int = TRUE.

What is read

One series per stratum, each point a row: the time, the estimate, censored where the row is censored, and, when the band is drawn, yMin and yMax. Censoring is read whether or not the marks are drawn, as it is from a Base R plot: it is part of the estimate, not of its decoration.

survminer

A figure from survminer::ggsurvplot() is read the same way when it is handed to show() or save_html() as it stands: its curve, band and censoring marks are redrawn as one maidr_survival() layer from the data the figure carries. The risk table, and a figure whose curve is not a survival probability (fun = "event" or "cumhaz"), are not read; the first is left out, the second keeps the reading geom_step() has.

See also

maidr_roc() and maidr_volcano(), the other declarations; save_html() and show() for rendering the declared chart

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- survival::survfit(
    survival::Surv(time, status) ~ sex,
    data = survival::lung
  )

  km <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    maidr_survival(fit, conf.int = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Days", title = "Survival by sex")

  # The same curves drawn with `geom_step()` read as a step chart: the
  # levels, and nothing of who was censored.
  if (interactive()) {
    show(km)
  }
}
